description: To let a reader filter by country, then region, then city, a report usually stacks three slicers, or one native hierarchy slicer that shows a long tree of checkboxes. Either way the reader opens lists to find their way, and nobody can tell at a glance what is selected. Chip Slicer Hierarchy puts the whole hierarchy in one visual, as chips. Click a country to filter; open it to see its regions next to it; the path to whatever is selected stays highlighted, so the reader always knows where they are. The field order in the Categories well is the hierarchy: adding a level is adding a field. WHAT YOU GET (FREE) • Up to three levels, single or multi-select, and leaf-only selection when parent levels are for navigation only • Expand and collapse, with optional auto-collapse of sibling branches • Colours per level for inactive, active and the ancestors of the selection • A measure on each chip, in the model's own format (dynamic format strings included) • Optional image on each chip, from images embedded in your model • Clear button (✕) and an "All" chip • Default selection: the first value, or the values you type ("Spain, France") • Six style templates — Classic, Outline, Soft, Square, One colour, Dark • On-object formatting, keyboard navigation (arrows, Right opens a level, Left closes it), screen readers and high-contrast themes • 12 languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese, French,…
